author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The raw rst_raw_n directly releases flops in two asynchronous clock domains, and set_false_path removes the only recovery and removal check, so neither release is synchronised or timed.

author_reading.rationale: rst_raw_n releases clk_a and clk_b flops directly with no synchroniser, and the false path only removes the timing check; the design relies on that check.

labels.rationale: The raw top-level rst_raw_n is released directly into two asynchronous clock domains with no synchroniser. set_false_path on rst_raw_n removes the recovery and removal checks that would expose this, and RDC-027 says a false path does not establish safety.
The false path cuts reset timing while the raw input directly releases two asynchronous domains. A release near either capture edge can leave that domain in an indeterminate state.
labels.suspected_flaw: The direct q_a to q_b data path is a separate uncontained CDC.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and the sites. The class follows B and the author: the case is about a false path hiding an unsynchronised release (RDC-027 together with RDC-003, as A lists). RDC-002 and RDC-013 (B) are inventory or run-level.
